clue.text: Man who painted factories across main road

indicators.note: the factories stretch across the road, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: mills are factories, as in cotton mills
the A1 is Britain's longest main road, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A painter is pictured working in the industrial landscape beside a busy trunk road.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the Great North Road in Britain; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Everett Millais was a Pre-Raphaelite painter, so he is a man who painted.

clue.text: Bird and donkey seen across river

indicators.note: the donkey is seen stretched across the river, so one goes round the other

parts.note: moke is slang for a donkey
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A bird and a donkey are glimpsed on the far side of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The mopoke is an Australasian owl named for its call.

clue.text: The Italian goes after fast food

indicators.note: goes after means the Italian article is placed after the other piece

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian chases after some fast food.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentil is an edible pulse, a staple food.

clue.text: Saw dad in strange hat, trim having bit of gold in it

indicators.note: in means the word for dad goes inside the jumbled hat
strange signals the letters of hat rearranged

parts.note: pop is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: having it in it means the gold letter sits inside the trim

parts.note: a hem is the trimmed edge of cloth

indicators.note: bit of takes just the first letter of gold

explanation.surface: Dad wears an odd hat, its brim edged with a touch of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb or a tool but means a proverb; 'strange' turns hat into AHT so dad can sit after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, which is what an apophthegm is.

clue.text: Great meal one page brought out

indicators.note: brought out means one letter is taken out of the meal

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A great meal is served once a page boy brings it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal for great or excellent.

clue.text: Revolutionary infiltrating mad groups

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy or mad
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A radical is pictured sneaking into crazy factions.
explanation.definitionFit: Batches are sets of things or people dealt with together, so groups is a synonym.

clue.text: Smart on top, is that woman in rubber?

indicators.note: on top means the first piece sits above the rest in this down entry

parts.note: to smart is to sting or burn
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A woman in rubber looks smart on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A burnisher is a tool or person that polishes by rubbing.

clue.text: Who perhaps shows merit, old whizz

indicators.note: to whizz is to whirl about, so these letters spin into a new order

explanation.surface: An old whizz-kid shows his worth.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is a long-running British TV science-fiction series.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Who is a Time Lord, so a Time Lord is a Who, perhaps.

clue.text: Abusive stuff coming in torrent — troublemaker getting maiden trapped

indicators.note: coming in means these pieces enter the word for torrent

parts.note: a hail of things is a torrent of them
Ate was the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin
m is the cricket abbreviation for maiden over

explanation.surface: A troublemaker traps a girl amid a torrent of abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped' also says the troublemaker and maiden sit inside the torrent.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate mail is abusive letters or messages sent to someone.

clue.text: Endless struggle concluded by small examination

indicators.note: concluded by means the next piece is placed at the end
endless means the final letter of the struggle is lost

parts.note: a scrum is a disorderly struggle
tiny means small

explanation.surface: An endless struggle ends with a small test.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutiny is close examination.

clue.text: Soldier quietly qualifying for £200 in board game?

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
in Monopoly you collect £200 when you pass or land on Go, so being on Go qualifies you

explanation.surface: A soldier quietly earns his £200 while playing Monopoly.
explanation.walkthrough: Monopoly is the property-trading board game whose Go square pays £200 in the British edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pongo is old British slang, chiefly naval, for a soldier or marine.

clue.text: Man in serial denial crosses mud going over boundary

indicators.note: crosses means stretches across, so the man's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: the apostle Peter denied knowing Jesus three times

indicators.note: going over is read as turning over, so this word runs backwards

parts.note: mire is deep mud

explanation.surface: A man who keeps denying things wades through mud to cross a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: The perimeter is the outer edge or boundary line of an area.

clue.text: Spooner gets to listen to woolly type — his radical contemporary

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of pairs of words, so the two words trade first sounds

parts.note: to hear is to listen
a cardie is a woolly cardigan

explanation.surface: Spooner's mangled phrase about listening to a knitwear wearer turns into a fellow Victorian.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap is by sound: hear cardie becomes Keir Hardie. 'His' refers to Spooner, who lived at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: Keir Hardie, founder of the Labour Party, was a radical politician living in Spooner's era.

clue.text: Some solvers may love it; some others mutter

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Crossword lovers are split: some relish a risque clue while others grumble at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is indecent or bawdy material, which some solvers enjoy in a clue and others frown on.

clue.text: Something potentially creaky to baffle the bosses?

parts.note: to floor someone is to baffle them
the board is a company's directors, its bosses

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to confuse their senior management.
explanation.definitionFit: Floorboards notoriously creak when walked on.

clue.text: Bad man attending place of worship, posing as an impressive leader?

parts.note: a church is a place of worship
ill means bad, as in ill luck
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A villain attends church while pretending to be a great statesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchillian describes behaviour modelled on Winston Churchill, the stirring wartime prime minister.

clue.text: Right form of book to enthral any number in translation

indicators.note: to enthral is to captivate, read as holding the letter inside

parts.note: an edition is a particular form of a book
n stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: The right version of a book captivates many readers in translation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is a rendering or translation of a text.

clue.text: Comedian in area besieged by ladies and gentlemen?

indicators.note: besieged by means surrounded, so the area goes inside the toilets

parts.note: public toilets are signed Ladies and Gentlemen, so these are WCs
a field is an area

explanation.surface: A comic plays to a field of ladies and gentlemen.
explanation.definitionFit: W. C. Fields was an American film comedian.

clue.text: Alien had a nice estate

indicators.note: alien means foreign or strange, so these letters become a different arrangement

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial owned a pleasant property.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Sports club facility — it's about danglin' dress?

parts.note: c (circa) means about
hangin' is a clipped form of hanging, which means dangling
to groom is to dress or tidy oneself

explanation.surface: A sports club facility is pictured, with clothes dangling and people dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in danglin' tells you the synonym also drops its final G.
explanation.definitionFit: Changing rooms are where players change kit at a sports club.

clue.text: Composer to deal with sounds

indicators.note: sounds means the word is said aloud, matching the composer's name

parts.note: to handle something is to deal with it

explanation.surface: A composer must cope with musical sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was the German-born Baroque composer of Messiah.

clue.text: A university lecturer is a lord

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A university academic is a peer.
explanation.walkthrough: The name Adonis comes from the Semitic word adon, meaning lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis derives from a Phoenician title meaning lord or master.

clue.text: One bird's losing the way, one bird

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: losing means the named letters are taken away

parts.note: the possessive is read as the plural birds
rd is short for road, a way

explanation.surface: A lost bird is pictured, straying from its path.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-billed wading bird, so it is one example of a bird.

clue.text: Legendary German greeting bald nerd, nastily

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: nastily signals the letters are rearranged badly

explanation.surface: Someone rudely greets a bald geek.
explanation.definitionFit: Hildebrand is a hero of early Germanic legend, as in the Hildebrandslied.

clue.text: Doctor sure to run out of words

parts.note: yup is a casual yes, meaning sure

explanation.surface: A doctor is certain to be lost for words.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry up is to forget one's lines and fall silent.

clue.text: See 6
Smoke close to Yorkshire river captured by historian

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the river pieces go within the historian

parts.note: Livy was the Roman historian
on can mean close to, as in a house on the river
the Don is a river in South Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Smoke rises near a Yorkshire river while a historian takes it captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Smoke' is a British nickname for London, and London ivy was a name for its thick fog.
explanation.definitionFit: London ivy was a Victorian nickname for the dense smoky fog of the capital.

clue.text: Poet has classy port brought round

indicators.note: brought round means the port encircles the other piece

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen
U means upper class, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

explanation.surface: A poet is offered a classy glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class comes from 1950s British usage, U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet.

clue.text: Relief when fools get sent back and put inside

indicators.note: put inside signals the word and goes within the other piece
sent back means reversed, so the word for fools runs backwards

parts.note: nits is slang for fools

explanation.surface: Fools are sent packing and locked up, bringing relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief is a substitute who takes over a duty, just like a stand-in.

clue.text: Doesn't get deeply involved with canoes?

definitions.meaning: one who ... stays in the shallows rather than swimming deep
the blades used to propel canoes

explanation.definitionFit: To paddle is to wade in shallow water, and paddles are the oars that drive a canoe.
